checks.text: With the default 2x2 matrices A = [[1,2],[3,4]] and B = [[5,6],[7,8]] and the operation select set to "Add", the result table shows the values 6, 8, 10, 12 in the cells at row 1 col 1, row 1 col 2, row 2 col 1, and row 2 col 2 respectively.

Changing the operation select to "Multiply" with the same default matrices updates the result table to show 19, 22, 43, 50 in the cells at row 1 col 1, row 1 col 2, row 2 col 1, and row 2 col 2 respectively.
Clicking the button "Copy result" copies the text "6 8 10 12" to the clipboard when the operation is "Add" and the default matrices are in use.
Changing the dimension select from "2x2" to "3x3" adds a third row and column to both matrix input grids, and the result table displays a 3x3 grid of zeros.
With the operation set to "Add" and matrices A = [[1,2],[3,4]] and B = [[5,6],[7,8]], clicking the button "Undo" reverts the last edit to a matrix cell, restoring the previous value in that cell.

Reload keeps the matrices and operation: after setting the operation to "Multiply" and editing cell A11 to "10", reloading the page shows the operation select set to "Multiply" and cell A11 containing "10".

With the operation set to "Multiply" and matrices of incompatible dimensions (e.g., A is 2x2 and B is 2x3 after manual dimension change), the result area shows the message "Dimensions do not match for multiplication".
